newsitem.title: USA: Southern Peru goes ahead with expansion.
newsitem.headline: Southern Peru goes ahead with expansion.

text.p: Southern Peru Copper Corp said Monday directors approved the expansion of the company's Cuajone copper mine.
The mine expansion will be the first stage of a multiyear expansion which will expand Cuajone's annual copper production by 71,000 short tons, the company said.

It said engineering for the second stage, modernization of the Ilo smelter, will begin immediately. Following completion of preliminary engineering and securing of financing, Southern Peru said, it plans to modernize the existing smelter to increase capacity and meet environmental guidelines.
The company said a future opportunity exists for a third stage of the modernization and expansion, consisting of a second Cuajone expansion and expansion of Ilo's capacity.
It said this will be evaluated later and will depend on availability of financing and other conditions at the time.
Southern Peru said the mine expansion is made possible by new ore reserves identified during its on-going exploration program.
At current rates of production, the Toquepala mine has a remaining life of 20 years, the Cuajone mine 55 years and leaching operations 19 years.

As of June 30, it said, Cuajone reserves have been increased to 1.27 billion tons with an average grade of 0.69 percent copper from the 968 million tons grading 0.72 percent reported as the end of 1995.
It said stage pme expansion at Cuajone will increase daily ore production to 96,000 tons from 64,000 tons and annual copper production to 216,500 tons from 145,500 tons.

Southern Peru said the mine expansion's capital cost is estimated to be $245 million, and construction is expected to begin early next year and be completed within two years. The project will begin once financing has been arranged, it said.
The company said the Ilo engineering studies will take place over the next 15 months and be followed by a three year construction period.
The modernization will be sequenced beginning with installation of a single line flash smelting furnace with a capacity of 1.25 million tons of concentrate per year.
Southern Peru said an operational advantage will be its ability to operating existing furnaces while the new furnace is brought on-line, thereby maintaining normal production.
The cost is expected to be about $787 million and once the project is completed, the smelter will meet current international environmental guidelines.
The company said it is now in the process of arranging long term financing for the expansion program.
Southern Peru is 54.1 percent owned by ASARCO Inc, 15.0 percent by Marmon Corp, 13.9 percent by Phelps Dodge Corp and 17.0 percent by common shareholders.
